name: Flats at Sand Creek
headline: Lincoln Avenue Communities is building Flats at Sand Creek, 144 two- to four-bedroom apartments for households at or below 60% AMI in six three-story buildings on 6.94 acres at the northeast corner of Peterson Road and North Carefree Circle, across from Sand Creek High School in northeast Colorado Springs. It won a 2025 federal 4% credit award from CHFA backed by up to $31.15M of El Paso County bonds.
why_it_matters: The project was allowed by existing R-5 zoning and approved administratively. It survived appeals to the Planning Commission (6-2) and City Council (7-2) over traffic and neighborhood fit, a by-right path worth noting for other infill sites. It also pairs a $4.05M Prop 123 land banking award with county bond cap.

status.label: Under construction (groundbreaking December 2025; foundations under way February 2026)
status.detail: El Paso County adopted the bond resolution (No. 25-284) on 2025-10-21. CSI Construction Company posted on 2025-12-08 that it had broken ground, and KOAA reported on 2026-02-10 that crews were laying foundations. The note closing date and completion date are not public.

next_step: Watch for building permits and vertical construction, then lease-up timing; also the Peterson Road school zone and signal changes the city has discussed.

background.text: In 2002 conditions of record limited the site to a religious institution, which was never built. On 2021-10-12 City Council removed those conditions (R-5 with airport overlay) for a 72-townhome concept that never got permits. The Gazette reports Lincoln then bought the land.

City Planning staff approved the development plan (DEPN-24-0133) administratively on 2025-02-24, with an administrative adjustment (ADRF-24-0073) for an 8-foot wall on the north edge in response to neighbors.

Neighbors appealed. The Planning Commission upheld the approval on 2025-04-09 (APPL-25-0003; 6-2 per the Gazette), and City Council denied the further appeal 7-2 on 2025-07-08 (APPL-25-0004). Concerns were traffic and pedestrian safety at Carefree and Peterson, views and neighborhood fit. School District 49 supported the project.

A traffic study was not required because the use was allowed by zoning, but the developer ran two (June 2024 and April 2025). The second showed more impact but no change in the intersection's risk level.

The county adopted Resolution 25-284 on its 2025-10-21 consent calendar, approving the borrower loan agreement, funding loan agreement and tax regulatory agreement. The county says it has no repayment obligation on the conduit note.
Lincoln Avenue said the project had also received more than $20 million in federal funding (likely the 4% credits; inferred).

discrepancies.text: The county's agenda memo says the required public hearing was held on 2025-09-05, while the draft bond resolution says the hearing notice was published on 2025-09-05 and the hearing was conducted on 2025-08-21.

The Gazette reports that Lincoln purchased the land, while the development plan and the city's appeal staff report list Carefree Landowner LLC as property owner, and the Prop 123 land banking award went to Fairview Housing Partners Ltd.
The draft resolution names the borrower Flats at Sand Creek LP, while the draft borrower loan agreement describes it as a limited liability company organized under Colorado law.

open_questions: Note closing date and amount actually funded; whose bond cap made up the $31.15M (county, Colorado Springs and Fountain assignments, statewide balance).

Relationship between Carefree Landowner LLC, Fairview Housing Partners and Lincoln Avenue, and how the Prop 123 money is structured (land purchase, ground lease or the bracketed $1M subordinate loan).
Final subordinate loans (the draft brackets $1M and $500,000), tax credit investor, equity price and total development cost.
Building permit records, expected completion and lease-up dates.
Rents; the project statement and award show only bedroom and AMI mix.
